commits.subject: Add the new test to the list
Fall back to the message body when the formatted body has nothing to render
commits.body:
The HTML sanitiser in toHtmlDocument() drops every tag outside its safelist,
which does not include img. A formatted body whose only content is an image —
a custom emoji, or a bot posting an image inline — therefore cleans down to an
empty document, and because that document is not null the ?: body fallbacks in
the timeline item factory, the room list preview, the notification resolver and
plainText are all dead. The message renders as an empty bubble.

Return null from toHtmlDocument() when no text survives the sanitisation, so the
existing fallbacks take the plain text body, which for these messages carries the
alt text the sender provided.

commits.subject: Rank the mention suggestions by how well they match what was typed
commits.body:
The member suggestions were emitted in whatever order the room member list
happened to be in, so a member who only matches somewhere in the middle of
their name could be offered above one whose name starts with the query.

Matches are now ordered by how well they match: display name prefix first,
then user ID localpart prefix, then any other match. The sort is stable, so
members of equal rank keep the order the member list gave them.

The @room suggestion was also matched case sensitively, so typing @Ro or
@ROOM dropped it while @ro kept it. It now matches the query the same way
the members do.

commits.subject: Name a sender the timeline has no profile for from the room member list
commits.body:
The timeline renders a message with the sender's raw Matrix ID whenever the
SDK has no profile for them, even though the room member list the same screen
already holds usually knows their display name and avatar.

The timeline item factory now falls back to the room member for a sender whose
profile is not resolved, both when the item is first built and when the member
list arrives afterwards, so the name and the avatar settle on the display name
instead of staying on the ID.

commits.subject: Keep the thread of a message that has been deleted
commits.body:
Deleting a message that headed a thread took the thread with it: the "N
replies" summary under the message disappeared and there was no way back to
the replies, which are still there.

Every branch of the timeline content mapper passes `MsgLikeContent`'s thread
information on except the redacted one, which returned a bare
`RedactedContent` and dropped it. The thread summary lives on
`MsgLikeContent` next to `kind`, so it survives the redaction; only the app
was throwing it away. `RedactedContent` now carries the thread info like the
other contents do, and `EventTimelineItem.threadInfo()` reads it.

A deleted message that still heads a thread is also left out of the "N
removed messages" group, which would otherwise hide the summary again as soon
as three deletions ended up next to each other.

Part of #7397

commits.subject: Offer conversations in the system share sheet
commits.body:
Sharing from another app listed Element X once, with no way to pick a
conversation: the Direct Share row never showed any.

The app already publishes a long-lived, conversation-categorised shortcut per
room, which is most of what the sharing shortcuts API needs. The part that was
missing is the declaration that ties those shortcuts to the share intent: the
launcher activity had no `android.app.shortcuts` meta-data, so there was no
`<share-target>` for the system to match them against.

It now ships one, matching the activity that already receives ACTION_SEND, and
the shortcuts carry the category it names.

The system offers these from Android 10 onwards, where sharing shortcuts are
handled natively. Reaching further back would additionally need the
androidx.sharetarget library, which is not added here.

Part of #3835

commits.subject: Do not open the editor when finishing the release
commits.body:
`git flow release finish` opened the editor three times, and the content was
never edited: twice for the merge commits, where the message generated by git is
always kept, and once for the message of the annotated tag, where a placeholder
was typed by hand. The last tags carry the message "tag" for that reason.

GIT_MERGE_AUTOEDIT=no keeps the merge messages git already generates, and -m
provides the tag message. git flow appends the tag name to that message, so the
tag of the next release will read "Release v26.09.0".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Only track read receipts on message-like events (#7361)
commits.body:
Ask the SDK to track receipts on message-like events only, for the live
timeline and for the focused and threaded ones, so all three agree. The
disabled case for the media and pinned-event timelines is unchanged. 

This matches the behaviour on Element X iOS.

The SDK attaches the receipt to the preceding event rather than the next
one, which is the placement its API offers.

commits.subject: Stop rescanning message bodies for emoji only on every recomposition (#7531)
commits.body:
Deciding whether a text message is emoji only compares the formatted body to
the plain one and runs a grapheme scan over the whole message. Nothing was
remembered, so both ran again on every recomposition of every visible message.

Remember the decision against the body and the formatted body. The preview
branch moves into the same computation, so the composable wrapper around
containsOnlyEmojis, which had a single caller and existed only to read
LocalInspectionMode, is no longer needed.
